tools_helpful.evidence: Bulk Windows.UI.Xaml -> Microsoft.UI.Xaml rewrite and scaffold succeeded; build ultimately SUCCEEDED with all 7 scenarios migrated (migration-score 100/7-of-7-pass).

tool_limitations.limitation: Only rewrites the Windows.UI.Xaml namespace prefix. It does NOT rewrite the sibling Windows.UI.* (non-Xaml) namespaces (Windows.UI.Colors, Windows.UI.Text, Windows.UI.Core dispatcher), so types used unqualified (e.g. Colors) break with CS0103 until a using Microsoft.UI; is added.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Document the Windows.UI -> Microsoft.UI (non-Xaml) move as a named common build error, not only as a row in a large namespace table.

special_apis.special_handling: Must stay on the Windows.Web.Http (WinRT) types after migration. IHttpFilter.SendRequestAsync has the signature IAsyncOperationWithProgress<HttpResponseMessage, HttpProgress> SendRequestAsync(HttpRequestMessage) where all types are Windows.Web.Http. Do NOT port to System.Net.Http: AdaptiveMediaSource request modification (auth headers, query params, HDCP) is built on Windows.Web.Http.Filters.IHttpFilter.

errors_encountered.error: CS0104: 'HttpClient' / 'HttpRequestMessage' / 'HttpResponseMessage' is an ambiguous reference between 'System.Net.Http.*' and 'Windows.Web.Http.*' (multiple files: ContentSelector, AdaptiveMediaSourceHttpFilterLogger, Scenario2-7)
errors_encountered.root_cause: The WinUI 3 scaffold enables <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>, which adds a global 'using System.Net.Http;'. UWP networking code uses Windows.Web.Http types, so any file that also brings System.Net.Http into scope (implicit global + an explicit using) sees two HttpClient/HttpRequestMessage/HttpResponseMessage types.
errors_encountered.fix: Keep the Windows.Web.Http using and remove the conflicting System.Net.Http using in those files (or add a using-alias, e.g. using HttpClient = Windows.Web.Http.HttpClient;). A file-level using wins over the ImplicitUsings global, so an explicit 'using Windows.Web.Http;' plus dropping the System.Net.Http using resolves it.

errors_encountered.error: CS0535: 'AdaptiveMediaSourceHttpFilterLogger' / 'AddAuthorizationHeaderFilter' does not implement interface member 'IHttpFilter.SendRequestAsync(HttpRequestMessage)'
errors_encountered.root_cause: Downstream of the CS0104 ambiguity: with System.Net.Http in scope, the HttpRequestMessage/HttpResponseMessage in the method signature bound to the System.Net.Http types, so the SendRequestAsync override no longer matched the Windows.Web.Http IHttpFilter contract.
errors_encountered.fix: Resolve the Http namespace ambiguity (above) so the method signature uses Windows.Web.Http.HttpRequestMessage / HttpResponseMessage; the interface member then matches.

errors_encountered.error: CS0103: The name 'Colors' does not exist in the current context (LogView.xaml.cs)
errors_encountered.root_cause: UWP exposes Colors via Windows.UI.Colors and the code used it unqualified. The Initialize rewrite only remaps Windows.UI.Xaml, not Windows.UI, so after migration no namespace brought 'Colors' into scope.
errors_encountered.fix: Add 'using Microsoft.UI;' (the WinUI 3 home of Colors / ColorHelper). Same applies to other unqualified Windows.UI.* helpers (Colors, ColorHelper, FontWeights via Microsoft.UI.Text).

dev_agent_struggles.where: Networking files across ContentSelector + Scenario2-7 + AdaptiveMediaSourceHttpFilterLogger
dev_agent_struggles.symptom: Repeated CS0104 ambiguity and cascading CS0535 interface-not-implemented across many files
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: ImplicitUsings global System.Net.Http colliding with the UWP Windows.Web.Http types the AdaptiveMediaSource/IHttpFilter API requires
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Removed System.Net.Http usings / kept Windows.Web.Http in the affected files
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: A named 'Windows.Web.Http vs System.Net.Http ambiguity' entry in MIGRATION-PATTERNS 'Common build errors' telling the agent to keep Windows.Web.Http for IHttpFilter/AdaptiveMediaSource code and drop the System.Net.Http using.

dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: Windows.UI (non-Xaml) namespace not rewritten by the script; type used unqualified
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Calling out the Windows.UI -> Microsoft.UI (non-Xaml) move and the 'add using Microsoft.UI;' fix as a named common build error.
